title: Flower listing on a dispensary shelf
description: One cannabis FLOWER product currently listed by one licensed dispensary. Flower only — whole bud. Pre-rolls, vapes, concentrates, hash, edibles, tinctures and topicals are out of scope even though some are made from flower. No prices: this project does not compare cost, and collecting price data would turn it into a price aggregator, which is both outside its purpose and the part of a menu platforms defend hardest.

listingId.description: Stable within one dispensary: slug of brand + strain. Re-derived on every capture, so the same shelf item keeps its identity across snapshots.

licenseNumber.description: The dispensary this was seen at. Must match a record in data/dispensaries.json.

capturedAt.description: When the shelf was read. Shelf contents go stale within hours — a listing without this is unusable, and the UI must always show it.

strainNameRaw.description: Exactly as printed on the menu, including punctuation and numbering: 'Gelato #33', 'Blue Dream '. Never cleaned up in this field.

strainNameCanonical.description: Normalized for matching: lowercase, '#' dropped, spacing collapsed — 'gelato 33'. Null when the raw name cannot be confidently resolved to a known strain, which is common for house crosses.

brand.description: The cultivator. As important as the strain name: the same genetics grown by two people is two different products by taste, which is why a recommendation keyed on strain alone is approximate.

brandKey.description: The cultivator's identity, derived from `brand` so the same operation is one thing across shops. The register stores a brand exactly as each shop prints it, which is right — `brand` is evidence — but it means ElectraLeaf arrives as six spellings (ElectraLeaf, Electraleaf, ELECTRALEAF, Electra Leaf, ElectraLeaf NY, Electraleaf NY) and one outreach target splits six ways. Derived by: strip accents, lowercase, drop everything but letters and digits, and remove the corporate and category words a shop may or may not print — cannabis, co, company, farm(s), lab(s), brand(s), ny, nyc, llc, inc. Across 9,542 listings that collapses 673 spellings to 398 cultivators. Null when the menu states no brand, and null rather than empty when normalization leaves nothing: a key of "" would silently merge every anonymous listing.

lineage.description: As stated by the menu. UNKNOWN when the menu does not say — never inferred from the strain's reputation.

terpenes.description: The sensory core of the record, and the field most often missing. `source` decides how a recommendation built on it may be phrased, so it is required and never guessed.

source.description: LAB_COA: from this batch's certificate of analysis — the only measurement of what is actually in this jar. MENU_LISTING: percentages the menu states without a linked COA. STRAIN_REFERENCE: the strain's typical profile from the reference table, NOT this batch — a recommendation on this basis is a sensory expectation, not a measurement, and must be presented as such. NONE: nothing known.

profile.description: Empty when source is NONE. Ordered by percent descending where percentages exist.

name.description: Controlled vocabulary. Menus spell these many ways — 'β-Caryophyllene', 'Beta-Caryophyllene', 'b caryophyllene' all normalize to CARYOPHYLLENE. CARYOPHYLLENE_OXIDE is deliberately separate from CARYOPHYLLENE: it is the oxidation product that accumulates as flower ages, and it reads woody and medicinal rather than peppery, so folding it into its parent would report a cured jar as a fresh one.

rawName.description: The spelling used on the source. Required in practice when name is OTHER, so an unmapped terpene is recoverable rather than lost.

percent.description: Percent by weight. Null when the source names a terpene without quantifying it — a common case worth keeping, since presence still carries sensory information.

referenceStrain.description: Which reference entry the fallback profile came from. Required when source is STRAIN_REFERENCE, so a reader can see what the expectation was based on.

packagedOn.description: Freshness materially changes terpene content: volatile terpenes evaporate over months. An old package will not taste like its COA.

availableSizesGrams.description: Recorded only when the menu gives it for free, e.g. [3.5, 7, 28]. Kept without price so a reader can see a strain exists only by the ounce. Never a reason to make an extra request.

productUrl.description: The product's own page on the shop's menu, absolute. Accepted only when the menu states a URL or a root-relative path; a bare slug is dropped rather than built into a link that may not exist. This is the route to a batch id, and therefore the difference between a collected terpene panel being a lead and being a record.

description.description: The menu's own copy for this product, tags stripped and whitespace collapsed, otherwise verbatim. Rule 5 in the source hierarchy: written to sell, corroboration only, and NEVER a lone source for a lineage, an aroma or an effect. It is captured because menu copy routinely states parentage and sensory notes for cultivars no aggregator covers, and it costs nothing to take at collection time — but a curator reading it must treat it as a claim by the seller, not a fact about the plant. Null when the menu gives none.

branch.description: Which of a chain's shops this shelf was read for, when the site remembers the chosen shop itself instead of naming it in the address — the option as the site worded it, e.g. 'Union Square 835 Broadway, NY, NY'. Absent when the address alone names the menu. Two listings on one address with different branches are two shelves, not one shared shelf.
